URI, the College of Health Sciences, Department of Nutrition and Food Sciences, and the FG Program are committed to Diversity, Equity, Inclusion, and Justice.
Students receive training in these areas as a part of coursework in several classes such as NFS 506, NFS 507, NFS 524, NFS 580.
Specific activities related to cultural competence are included in the clinical/community experiential rotation (NFS 582) as well as NFS 507 and are evaluated to document satisfactory completion of the Future Education Model (FEM) Competency 1.7.
Self-assessment and professional development are an integral part of the FG.
Students complete portfolios for clinical, community, and foodservice management rotations to document projects used for competency assessment.
Each of the three portfolios concludes with a self-evaluation section.

This self-evaluation section includes a self-evaluation of progress through the rotation as well as progress in awareness of cultural, equity, and bias issues.
Students conclude with a plan to develop strengths and address areas for improvement.
FG Mission Statement: The University of Rhode Island Dietetics Future Education Model Graduate Program (FG) represents the successful integration of The University of Rhode Island and the healthcare-related facilities in the state.
The FG Program is committed to providing the opportunity for the practical application of theoretical knowledge in the area of dietetic practice and to training competent Registered Dietitian Nutritionists with demonstrated skills in community and population health.
The program provides a broad base of opportunities for learning by utilizing a variety of healthcare facilities and providing diverse didactic programs.
